In mathematics, the '''Deuring–Heilbronn phenomenon''', discovered by {{harvs|txt|first=Max|last=Deuring|year=1933|authorlink=Max Deuring}} and {{harvs|txt|first=Hans|last=Heilbronn|year=1934|authorlink=Hans Heilbronn}},  states that a counterexample to the [[generalized Riemann hypothesis]] for one [[Dirichlet L-function]] affects the location of the zeros of other Dirichlet L-functions.

* [[Siegel zero]]
